fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json` and
`src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` declare `trace_id` as `["string","null"]`,
described as "Langfuse trace id when tracing is enabled", but `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`
hardcodes `None` at every site emitting it. No per-run identity exists, so a verdict cannot
name its run and no header can carry a run-stable value.

## Approach

Mint one identity per gate run at the two boundaries that already resolve the run's config
once: `workflow/gate_dispatch.py:167` (plan-review, `ctx.ticket_id` in scope) and `:762`
(completion-verifier). Both open `gate_config(cfg)`, whose contextvar every op reads via
`resolve_gate_config` (`config.py:99-107`). Attach with `dataclasses.replace(cfg, ...)` before
`gate_config(cfg)`, never mutating the caller's object.

Three values: `trace_id` (32 lowercase hex — the active OpenTelemetry span's trace id when one
is recording, else `secrets.token_hex(16)`), `ticket_id` (the boundary's own), and `operation`
(`"review-plan"` or `"verify-completion"` — rebar's canonical verb names, so the vocabulary
matches the CLI and docs). No `run_id`: `trace_id` already identifies the run. `ticket_id` and
`operation` are minted here because the boundary is the only place they are knowable; their
consumer is `26ae-041f-dcc4-4279`'s `${run:...}` vocabulary, and criteria below cover them.

32-hex is W3C trace-id format, which Langfuse v3+ requires. Reading a live span's id is correct
when an enclosing span exists and free when none does — but it does NOT by itself align the
header with rebar's exported spans: rebar opens no root span, so at the boundary nothing is
normally recording and the value is minted, while `tracing.py`'s per-candidate spans open later
inside each model request, each its own trace root. That alignment needs the run-level root
span, which is out of scope. Random per run, not derived from the ticket: a derived value would
merge every re-review into one trace.

The value reaches pool workers unchanged via `generation._submit_ctx`
(`copy_context().run`, `generation.py:154-165`), used by `pass1.py:426-427` and
`container_stage.py:260`.

Read `req.config.trace_id` at **all three** `runner.py` sites hardcoding `None`:

- `:254` — `FakeRunner.run`'s `mode == "structured"` branch, comment "Structured mode (e.g.
  verify_completion)". The completion verifier is structured-mode, so its fake verdict returns
  here, not `:259`; omitting it makes the completion criterion below unsatisfiable.
- `:259` — `FakeRunner.run`'s findings branch.
- `:719` — the real runner.

The two `FakeRunner` branches are selected by `req.mode`, so testing one says nothing about the
other. The seam is `req.config`: the gate config arrives as `RunRequest(config=...)`
(`operations.py:209-212`) and `FakeRunner` holds no instance config, reaching configuration only
via `req.config` (`repo_path` at `:264`). Derivations like `max_output_cfg` use
`dataclasses.replace`, so the identity rides through.

Both schema descriptions are restated in the same change so the contract cannot contradict the
emitted value: "per-gate-run correlation id (32 lowercase hex); null for deterministic or
fallback verdicts and standalone ops" — deliberately not "present inside any gate run". Other
emitters run inside a gate scope with no LLM call
(`workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py:153`, `completion_reconcile.py:252`,
`workflow/completion_failures.py:98`), and `spec_scan.py:138` is not a gate op; all stay `None`
and are out of scope, since a deterministic verdict has no gateway request behind it.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — the identity fields on `LLMConfig`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — mint at both run boundaries.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — read `req.config.trace_id` at `:254`, `:259`, `:719`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json` — restate the `trace_id` description.
- `src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` — restate the `trace_id` description.
- `tests/unit/test_run_correlation.py` (new) — the tests below.

## Testing

Tier: in-process unit tests plus schema validation — contextvar propagation and verdict field
population both run for real in-process; no subprocess or network boundary.

- Happy path: within one scope every `resolve_gate_config()` read returns the same `trace_id`.
- Edge: two scopes differ; the value is `None` outside any gate run.
- Concurrency: a value read inside a `_submit_ctx` pool task equals the submitting thread's.
- Real-runner path: `:719` driven through `PydanticAIRunner.run` with the offline
  `model_override` TestModel harness — every other verdict assertion is satisfiable through
  `FakeRunner`, leaving `:719` otherwise unproven.
- Both gate surfaces: each produces a verdict carrying the run's `trace_id`, validated against
  its own schema.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Inside one gate run `resolve_gate_config().trace_id` is identical across repeated reads;
      checked by asserting equality across three reads in one scope.
- [ ] Two gate runs produce different `trace_id` values; checked by a test over two scopes.
- [ ] `trace_id` is 32 lowercase hex; checked by `re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{32}", value)`.
- [ ] With a recording OpenTelemetry span active, `trace_id` equals that span's trace id as 32
      hex; checked by a test starting a real span and comparing.
- [ ] With no span recording, `trace_id` is freshly minted; checked by asserting two runs differ
      with no tracer configured.
- [ ] A value read inside a `_submit_ctx` pool task equals the submitting thread's.
- [ ] Within a gate scope `resolve_gate_config().ticket_id` and `.operation` equal what the
      boundary minted them from, with `operation` equal to `review-plan` and
      `verify-completion` respectively; checked for each boundary.
- [ ] A plan-review verdict carries the run's `trace_id` and validates against
      `review_result.schema.json`.
- [ ] A completion-verifier verdict produced in a completion-verifier scope carries that run's
      `trace_id` and validates against `completion_verdict.schema.json`.
- [ ] A verdict produced through the real runner site `:719` carries `req.config.trace_id`;
      checked by driving `PydanticAIRunner.run` with the offline `model_override` harness, so no
      `FakeRunner` branch can satisfy it.
- [ ] Both schema descriptions state the correlation id in 32-hex shape and the
      deterministic/fallback exemption, with no residual Langfuse claim and no "present inside
      any gate run" wording; checked by a grep over both files.
- [ ] A deterministic completion verdict produced inside a gate scope still carries
      `trace_id: null`; checked by driving the deterministic child-closure path.
- [ ] The identity survives a per-request config derivation; checked by asserting
      `max_output_cfg(cfg).trace_id == cfg.trace_id`.
- [ ] Outside any gate run the identity is `None` and verdicts are unchanged.
